original_target.title: Maximum total number of lines on a smooth complex surface

full_original_statement:
For an integer $`d`$, let $`\mathcal H_d`$ consist of every smooth degree-$`d`$ hypersurface $`X\subset\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)`$. A line means a complex projective line wholly contained in $`X`$, counted once as a geometric subset. The surface varies over all of $`\mathcal H_d`$.

Write $`L(X)`$ for the number of lines contained in $`X`$ and set

```math
L_d=\max_{X\in\mathcal H_d}L(X).
```


Determine $`L_d`$ for every integer $`d\ge5`$. In particular, determine the exact value of $`L_5`$.

These are finite attained integer maxima. There is no Fermat, symmetry, genericity or prescribed-configuration assumption, and intersecting lines are included.
queries: "lines surfaces" maxima (site:zenodo.org OR site:hal.science OR site:github.com)

sources.scope_comparison: The actual theorem constructs a smooth quintic pencil whose members have exactly 85 lines. This improves the lower bound for the maximum but does not prove 85 is an upper bound over all smooth quintics. Its introduction retains the general d>=5 extremum as unknown and cites the universal quintic upper bound 127. Counting skew lines on fixed Fermat surfaces changes both objective and class. No matching exact L5 or all-degree maximum announcement found.
